This eco-friendly grazing method is being embraced by renewable energy companies as a cost-effective way to manage vegetation, while farmers benefit from expansive grazing land without hefty property expenses.

After investing over 200 hours, they've constructed life-sized dinosaur replicas and an automated escape show, complete with grand entrance gates. Open to the public at no cost, this attraction fosters community spirit as neighbors flock to capture the experience and enjoy this festive installation.

Swisher noted that if Democrats regain control of Congress in upcoming elections, probes could restart. Additionally, she implied that Musk's political ties might shield him from scrutiny. Bernie Sanders has voiced his disapproval of Musk's extensive political expenditures, underscoring the risks of oligarchs meddling in the democratic process.

Abdul Latheef Naha speaks to investigators, psychiatrists and forensic experts to understand how did a homeless man become the target of a group that took it upon itself to punish him and such incidents are recurring.

The 18-year-old, facing a 1-2 deficit, demonstrated resilience and skill. Anahat will now go head-to-head with Malaysia's Sivasangari Subramaniam, reigniting their rivalry from the Asian Games final, solidifying her remarkable tournament journey in Redwood City.

The satellite-based network also supports the use of drones, which Ukraine deploys both to strike Russian targets and to defend against incoming attacks. Disruptions to connectivity can therefore affect the military's ability to operate drones and respond to Russian assaults.

Modi did not mention Netanyahu’s invitation in his post on the conversation. “We exchanged views on developments in West Asia and underscored the urgent need to restore peace and stability in the region,” Modi said on X.

description: PM Modi and his Polish counterpart Tusk expressed deepest concern in a joint statement over the war in Ukraine, including its tragic humanitarian consequences and the impact on Global South. In his media statement, Modi assured Tusk that whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every meaningful effort for peace.

title: From Jan 1, WhatsApp, Telegram won’t work without SIM cards, govt issues guidelines
description: The move is to curb cross-border cyber frauds, phishing, digital arrest scams using Indian mobile numbers and enhance telecom cyber security. Apple has updated iOS with a software patch to help detect when an iPhone is operating without a physical SIM card to abide with the rules. It is learnt Signal has not yet responded to govt notices.

description: Life insurance policies, too, would no longer be accepted as proof. Proposing sweeping changes to the driving licence (DL) regime under Motor Vehicles Rules, the road transport ministry Wednesday issued a draft notification to raise the pass mark for the online safe-driving tutorial assessment from the current 60% to 75%.

title: Centre flags data gap, regulatory hurdles in curbing hospital mark-ups
description: The Union govt has told the SC in its affidavit that margins on hospital consumables can range from 100% to 1,000% or more, highlighting concerns over the high mark-ups patients often face on supplies used during treatment. However, a senior official told TOI that the govt does not have the data needed to assess margins across hospital supplies and determine whether wider controls are warranted.

It also called for a ban or other action if justified under applicable law. The letter was also copied to the Union health and home ministries and the chairperson of National Medical Commission.

title: Don’t blindly follow foreign custody order: Supreme Court
description: A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan said cases already dealt with by foreign courts were coming before it time and again and their adjudication was not easy as they involved deeply emotional and sensitive issues. It added that the welfare of the child “must be understood in the widest sense, not by money or physical comfort alone”.

title: Sonia Gandhi makes Instagram debut, shares first look of her upcoming book
description: In her first post on Instagram, Sonia shared a video of her welcoming the first copies of her autobiography “Belonging: A journey of love” which is set to be released on Nov 10. The video showed her holding up the book and then sharing sweets with daughter and MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. “It is a story of love, duty, loss and finding a place to belong. I look forward to sharing it with you,” Sonia wrote on the post.

title: Will decide on any notice to remove CEC according to rules: LS Speaker Om Birla
description: Both the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha chairman had rejected previous notices from the opposition, saying their allegations “do not prima facie meet the high constitutional bar for removal proceedings”. Birla noted the process for removal of the chief election commissioner was the same as for removing a Supreme Court judge.

title: At least sixteen dead, 32 injured after 7.0 quake strikes China’s Tibet: State media
description: The epicentre of the quake, which struck at 10:33 p.m. (1433 GMT), was located in a mountainous area about 190 kilometres (120 miles) east-northeast of Nagqu, and 390 kilometres northeast of the regional capital Lhasa, says U.S. Geological Survey

title: Indian dies in Saudi airport strike; MEA slams infrastructure attacks
description: India has condemned the continued attacks on civilian and energy infrastructure. “These attacks have unfortunately resulted in civilian deaths and injuries. We convey our heartfelt condolences to the bereaved family and wish speedy recovery to those injured. The Indian embassy in Riyadh...will provide all possible assistance,” said ministry of external affairs (MEA) in a statement. The victim has not been identified by Saudi authorities so far.

title: Resignation by Justice Yashwant Varma may end Lok Sabha proceedings
description: Justice Yashwant Varma’s name still figuring on the list of judges on the HC website had bolstered the view. However, sources said legal opinion, backed by a court verdict, that an HC judge’s resignation comes into effect as soon as he resigns may prevail in what was earlier seen as a legal grey area.

title: MEA calls out UN report for saying Dawood Ibrahim's D-company India-based
description: First secretary in India’s permanent mission to UN, Raghoo Puri, was responding to a report by Ben Saul, the special rapporteur on the ‘Promotion and Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms while Countering Terrorism’. He said this presented member-states with a fait accompli, an unfortunate situation for an organisation already facing challenges to its legitimacy.

title: Hospitals ‘overcharging’ is a malpractice: Govt to Supreme Court
description: In an affidavit filed in SC on the issue of capping prices of all medicines and medical consumables, chemicals and fertilisers ministry said that patients have a very low bargaining position with respect to hospitals, resulting in various malpractices. The affidavit noted the irony of India being home to companies making cheap drugs but patients here having to pay way above the manufacturing price, as well as patients being subjected to overcharging by hospitals.

title: Use of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s deep fake videos to collect money: Rajasthan youth moves Madras High Court seeking bail
description: Justice N. Ramesh will hear on Friday the bail plea made by J. Shyabu Khan of Boontoli village in Alwar district

title: Only ‘sanatanis’ will touch Durga idols during immersion: Bengal CM Suvendu
description: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced that only those who believe in Sanatan Dharma can touch Durga idols during immersion. This directive aims to maintain the sanctity of traditional rituals amidst rising political tensions. Several opposition leaders criticized the decision, alleging it promotes religious exclusion and violates constitutional principles. The immersion involved the use of trolleys instead of cranes, which is a departure from previous practices.

title: Thousands gather in Paris after court lifts protest ban despite fears of new violence
description: The Paris prefecture previously said the ban was necessary, given the risk of street violence after groups of masked youth clashed with officers, looted shops and torched cars over the weekend

title: Delhi content creator arrested over racial abuse of Tripura youth
description: The Agartala police have registered a case and are expected to come to Delhi to investigate the matter, according to Additional Commissioner of Police (IFSO) Sanjay Bhatia

title: 21 years on, double life term for Jammu terror attack that killed baby, 2 others
description: In his order on Wednesday, principal sessions judge Ramban Ajay Kumar Gupta rejected defence arguments that the attack had taken place more than two decades ago when Sharief was young, his long incarceration and possibility of rehabilitation. Besides the life sentences, the court imposed two separate terms of 10 years on Sharief under various sections pertaining to murder and arms act offences.

title: Centre betrayed us, now want full statehood for Ladakh: Sonam Wangchuk
description: Wangchuk said the representatives of Leh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) had come prepared for Oct 22 talks in Delhi as a follow up of the May 15 meeting in Leh, with the expectation that the MHA and Ladakh bodies' respective drafts on contours and powers of UT-level body and district councils, would be discussed.

title: Amid attacks, sales surge at Kolkata Left bookstalls
description: Book stalls set up by Left parties saw significant sales increases during Durga Puja amid incidents of vandalism. The CPM stall at Jadavpur 8B bus stand recorded sales of Rs 16 lakh, nearly four times last year's figures. Despite attacks, sales for other Left stalls also increased, evidencing a broader engagement with literature. Politicians from various parties expressed solidarity with the Left stalls amidst ongoing disputes.

title: Red Corner Notice against Russian ‘who fled with child’
description: The Delhi Police have issued a Red Corner Notice for Russian citizen Viktoriia Basu due to alleged violations of child custody regulations. Viktoriia reportedly exited India with her son in defiance of a Supreme Court shared custody ruling. Extradition efforts are currently underway with Russian officials to find her. Furthermore, an associate, Natasha, is being investigated for allegedly facilitating her departure.

title: ‘Ridiculed for eating beef’ at school, 16-year-old Tamil Nadu boy dies by suicide
description: In Coimbatore, a tragic incident unfolded as 16-year-old A Akilan, a Scheduled Caste student, took his own life allegedly due to persistent harassment from peers and a teacher over his dietary preferences. His mother highlighted that repeated pleas to school officials were ignored, resulting in this heartbreaking event. Authorities have initiated a case against the teacher, headmaster, and two students, inciting public protests for justice and a thorough investigation.

title: PM Modi calls for stronger global institutions; takes ‘failed product’ jab at Cong
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi emphasized the need for stronger global institutions during his address at the NDTV World Summit. He argued that the current global system struggles to address new challenges, particularly in international relations. Modi also criticized Congress leadership for failing to effectively launch their leader, calling it a burden on the party. Furthermore, he highlighted India's role in international cooperation, especially during the Covid-19 pandemic.

title: CEC impeachment: Birla says fresh motion will be examined as per rules

Tom Brady donated $170,000 Salem State speaking fee to charities in 2015
description: Tom Brady collected $170,000 for a speaking gig at Salem State University, generously donating the entire sum to charity. He allocated $50,000 to Best Buddies and distributed the remaining funds to various other organizations. With approximately 4,000 attendees present, ticket sales effectively covered his speaking fee. However, the event was notable for Brady facing questions about the NFL's Deflategate saga. The university reported a financial profit from hosting the event.

title: Murray’s wife Kim Sears, four children: Inside his family life after retirement
description: Andy Murray has officially retired from professional tennis and, in doing so, has opened a new chapter in his life, and the former world No 1 will have more time to spend with his wife Kim Sears and their four children. From parenting and family routines to their shared business interests at Cromlix, the couple are handling life outside the demands of professional tennis while keeping family at the center.

title: BrahMos goes global, eyes next-gen missile by 2028; 1,500-km strike variant on radar
description: BrahMos Aerospace is set to develop the next-generation BrahMos-NG missile by 2027-28. The company aims to strengthen its supply chain and production capacity to meet increasing demand. Interest from foreign militaries in air-launched versions of BrahMos is growing. A 1,500-km-range variant is also under exploration but remains at a conceptual stage. Recent contracts with the Indian Navy are expected to boost domestic manufacturing and participation from local industries.

title: Giannis Antetokounmpo reportedly invested $70 million in real estate in 2025
description: Since October 2025, NBA superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo has strategically invested approximately $70 million in various real estate ventures. His family's company, Ante, has facilitated several significant purchases, including apartment complexes in Wisconsin, Brooklyn, and Chicago. Notably, he recently acquired a lavish $13.5 million mansion in Pinecrest, Florida, after joining the Miami Heat. These investments reflect Antetokounmpo's commitment to expanding his financial portfolio beyond basketball income.

title: Civil war & terror: Why Libya is still broken 15 yrs after Gaddafi's bloody end
description: Since the fall of Muammar Gaddafi in 2011, Libya has been trapped in a cycle of political strife and disunity. Although a UN-backed agreement was reached with hopes of conducting elections, various administrations maintain control over separate regions. By April 2026, a unified national budget was achieved, yet obstacles to effective implementation loom large.

title: Virginia teen's model improves simulated earthquake sensor coverage by 16.7%
description: A 14-year-old student from Williamsburg, Virginia, has become one of 30 finalists in a national science competition after developing a mathematical model to improve earthquake sensor placement. Isabel Rossi's six-month research project showed that adding just five sensors could increase simulated detection coverage by 16.7%. She used earthquake records from California and mathematical methods to identify better sensor locations.

title: After renaming Lake Ontario, Google CEO rejects US request to rename Atlantic Ocean
description: President Trump has recently proposed renaming the Atlantic Ocean, following prior discussions about the Atlantic Ocean. During a recent event, he mentioned contacting Google Maps regarding these renaming efforts. Google CEO Sundar Pichai reportedly declined his proposal on the grounds that oceans encompass multiple countries. This follows the US administration's earlier renaming of Lake Ontario to Lake America for US users.

title: 3 aircraft carriers, jets & troops: Israel, US plan to attack Iran after midterms
description: The United States and Israel are preparing for potential military strikes against Iran after the upcoming midterm elections. Iran has announced it will reveal a new weapon called the 'Father of All Bombs' as tensions rise. US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to discuss military options recently. Meanwhile, Iranian officials warn of severe responses if attacked, emphasizing improved missile capabilities.
